name: Amikacin

fields.mechanism_of_action: Amikacin is a semi-synthetic aminoglycoside antibiotic derived from kanamycin. As an aminoglycoside, amikacin binds to the prokaryotic ribosome and inhibits protein synthesis in susceptible bacteria, and it is bactericidal in vitro against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria (FDA label, Amikacin Sulfate Injection USP, Microbiology - Mechanism of Action). Amikacin resists degradation by certain aminoglycoside-inactivating enzymes that affect gentamicin, tobramycin and kanamycin, and in vitro studies show that amikacin sulfate combined with a beta-lactam antibiotic acts synergistically against many clinically significant Gram-negative organisms (FDA label, Microbiology - Mechanism of Resistance and Interaction with Other Antimicrobials).
indications: Amikacin Sulfate Injection: short-term treatment of serious infections due to susceptible strains of Gram-negative bacteria, including Pseudomonas species, Escherichia coli, indole-positive and indole-negative Proteus species, Providencia species, Klebsiella-Enterobacter-Serratia species and Acinetobacter (Mima-Herellea) species (FDA label, INDICATIONS AND USAGE)

Clinical studies have shown effectiveness in bacterial septicemia (including neonatal sepsis); serious infections of the respiratory tract, bones and joints, central nervous system (including meningitis) and skin and soft tissue; intra-abdominal infections (including peritonitis); and burns and post-operative infections (including post-vascular surgery); also in serious complicated and recurrent urinary tract infections due to these organisms (FDA label, INDICATIONS AND USAGE)

Aminoglycosides including amikacin are NOT indicated in uncomplicated initial episodes of urinary tract infections unless the causative organisms are not susceptible to antibiotics having less potential toxicity (FDA label, INDICATIONS AND USAGE)

Amikacin has also been shown to be effective in staphylococcal infections and may be considered as initial therapy in known or suspected staphylococcal disease such as severe infections where the causative organism may be either a Gram-negative bacterium or a staphylococcus, infections due to susceptible strains of staphylococci in patients allergic to other antibiotics, and mixed staphylococci/Gram-negative infections; in certain severe infections such as neonatal sepsis, concomitant therapy with a penicillin-type drug may be indicated (FDA label, INDICATIONS AND USAGE)

ARIKAYCE (amikacin liposome inhalation suspension), a separate inhaled liposomal product: indicated in adults who have limited or no alternative treatment options for the treatment of Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) lung disease as part of a combination antibacterial regimen in patients who do not achieve negative sputum cultures after a minimum of 6 consecutive months of a multidrug background regimen; approved under accelerated approval based on sputum culture conversion by Month 6, with clinical benefit not yet established, and not recommended for non-refractory MAC lung disease (FDA label, ARIKAYCE, section 1)
Kenya Essential Medicines List 2023 lists amikacin injection (50 mg/mL in 2 mL vial and 250 mg/mL in 2 mL vial) at level of use 4, i.e. for use at referral hospitals (KEML 2023, section 7.2.1.1)
contraindications: A history of hypersensitivity to amikacin is a contraindication for its use (FDA label, CONTRAINDICATIONS)

A history of hypersensitivity or serious toxic reactions to aminoglycosides may contraindicate the use of any other aminoglycoside because of the known cross-sensitivities of patients to drugs in this class (FDA label, CONTRAINDICATIONS)
ARIKAYCE: known hypersensitivity to any aminoglycoside (FDA label, ARIKAYCE, section 4)
side_effects: Neurotoxicity - ototoxicity: toxic effects on the eighth cranial nerve can result in hearing loss, loss of balance or both; amikacin primarily affects auditory function, and cochlear damage includes high-frequency deafness and usually occurs before clinical hearing loss can be detected (FDA label, ADVERSE REACTIONS - Neurotoxicity-Ototoxicity)

Neurotoxicity - neuromuscular blockade: acute muscular paralysis and apnea can occur following treatment with aminoglycoside drugs; neuromuscular blockade and respiratory paralysis have been reported after parenteral injection, topical instillation and oral use (FDA label, WARNINGS box and ADVERSE REACTIONS)

Nephrotoxicity: elevation of serum creatinine, albuminuria, presence of red and white cells, casts, azotemia and oliguria; renal function changes are usually reversible when the drug is discontinued, and reports of toxic nephropathy and acute renal failure have been received during postmarketing surveillance (FDA label, ADVERSE REACTIONS - Nephrotoxicity)

Other reactions reported on rare occasions: skin rash, drug fever, headache, paresthesia, tremor, nausea and vomiting, eosinophilia, arthralgia, anemia, hypotension and hypomagnesemia; macular infarction sometimes leading to permanent loss of vision has been reported after intravitreous administration (FDA label, ADVERSE REACTIONS - Other)

Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhoea (CDAD) has been reported with amikacin and may range in severity from mild diarrhoea to fatal colitis (FDA label, WARNINGS - Clostridium difficile associated diarrhea)

ARIKAYCE: hypersensitivity pneumonitis, hemoptysis, bronchospasm and exacerbation of underlying pulmonary disease; ototoxicity (deafness, dizziness, presyncope, tinnitus and vertigo) was reported in 17% of patients on ARIKAYCE plus background regimen versus 9.8% on background regimen alone, driven mainly by tinnitus (8.1% vs 0.9%) and dizziness (6.3% vs 2.7%); also anaphylaxis and hypersensitivity reactions, nephrotoxicity and neuromuscular blockade (FDA label, ARIKAYCE, sections 5.1-5.8 and 6.1)

dosage.adult: For adults, children and older infants with normal renal function: 15 mg/kg/day divided into 2 or 3 equal doses administered at equally divided intervals, i.e. 7.5 mg/kg every 12 hours or 5 mg/kg every 8 hours; treatment of patients in the heavier weight classes should not exceed 1.5 gram/day, and the total daily dose by all routes of administration should not exceed 15 mg/kg/day (FDA label, DOSAGE - Intramuscular Administration for Patients with Normal Renal Function). The usual duration of treatment is 7 to 10 days and it is desirable to limit the duration of treatment to short term whenever feasible; if definite clinical response does not occur within 3 to 5 days, therapy should be stopped and the susceptibility pattern rechecked. In uncomplicated urinary tract infections when amikacin is indicated, a dose of 250 mg twice daily may be used (FDA label, DOSAGE - Intramuscular Administration for Patients with Normal Renal Function). Intravenous administration uses identical individual, daily and cumulative doses: the contents of a 500 mg vial are added to 100 or 200 mL of sterile diluent and administered to adults over a 30 to 60 minute period (FDA label, DOSAGE - Intravenous Administration). Serum peak concentrations (30 to 90 minutes after injection) above 35 micrograms per mL and trough concentrations (just prior to the next dose) above 10 micrograms per mL should be avoided (FDA label, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION). ARIKAYCE: once daily inhalation of the contents of one 590 mg/8.4 mL vial using the Lamira Nebulizer System (FDA label, ARIKAYCE, section 2.2).
dosage.geriatric: Elderly patients may have reduced renal function which may not be evident in routine screening tests such as BUN or serum creatinine, so a creatinine clearance determination may be more useful, and monitoring of renal function during treatment with aminoglycosides is particularly important (FDA label, PRECAUTIONS - General). No specific geriatric dose reduction beyond renal-function-based adjustment is stated in the label. For ARIKAYCE, renal function should be monitored in patients with known or suspected renal impairment, including elderly patients with potential age-related decreases in renal function (FDA label, ARIKAYCE, section 8.7).
dosage.paediatric: Newborns: a loading dose of 10 mg/kg administered initially followed by 7.5 mg/kg every 12 hours (FDA label, DOSAGE - Intramuscular Administration for Patients with Normal Renal Function). Infants should receive a 1 to 2 hour infusion for intravenous administration, and the volume of fluid used depends on the amount of amikacin ordered, sufficient to infuse over a 30 to 60 minute period in paediatric patients (FDA label, DOSAGE - Intravenous Administration). Aminoglycosides should be used with caution in premature and neonatal infants because of renal immaturity and the resulting prolongation of serum half-life (FDA label, PEDIATRIC USE). ARIKAYCE: safety and effectiveness in pediatric patients have not been established (FDA label, ARIKAYCE, section 8.4).

interactions: Other neurotoxic or nephrotoxic products: concurrent and/or sequential systemic, oral or topical use should be avoided, particularly bacitracin, cisplatin, amphotericin B, cephaloridine, paromomycin, viomycin, polymyxin B, colistin, vancomycin or other aminoglycosides; advanced age and dehydration are additional risk factors (FDA label, WARNINGS box and PRECAUTIONS - General)

Potent diuretics: concurrent use of amikacin with ethacrynic acid or furosemide should be avoided, since diuretics by themselves may cause ototoxicity, and when administered intravenously diuretics may enhance aminoglycoside toxicity by altering antibiotic concentrations in serum and tissue (FDA label, WARNINGS box and PRECAUTIONS - General)

Cephalosporins: increased nephrotoxicity has been reported following concomitant parenteral administration of aminoglycosides and cephalosporins, and concomitant cephalosporins may spuriously elevate creatinine determinations (FDA label, PRECAUTIONS - General)

Beta-lactam antibiotics: in vitro mixing of aminoglycosides with penicillin or cephalosporin may result in significant mutual inactivation, with a reduction in serum half-life or serum level when the drugs are given by separate routes; inactivation is clinically significant only in patients with severely impaired renal function (FDA label, PRECAUTIONS - General)

Neuromuscular blocking agents and anaesthetics: neuromuscular blockade and respiratory paralysis have been reported, especially in patients receiving anaesthetics, neuromuscular blocking agents such as tubocurarine, succinylcholine or decamethonium, or massive transfusions of citrate-anticoagulated blood; calcium salts may reverse these phenomena but mechanical respiratory assistance may be necessary (FDA label, WARNINGS box)

ARIKAYCE: drugs with neurotoxic, nephrotoxic or ototoxic potential should be used with caution, and ethacrynic acid, furosemide, urea and mannitol are specifically cautioned against (FDA label, ARIKAYCE, sections 7.1 and 7.2)
fields.monitoring: Closely monitor renal and eighth-nerve function, especially in patients with known or suspected renal impairment at the onset of therapy and in those whose renal function is initially normal but who develop signs of renal dysfunction during therapy (FDA label, WARNINGS box). Monitor serum amikacin concentrations when feasible to assure adequate levels and to avoid toxic levels and prolonged peak concentrations above 35 micrograms per mL; avoid peak concentrations above 35 mcg/mL and trough concentrations above 10 mcg/mL (FDA label, WARNINGS box and DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION). Examine urine for decreased specific gravity, increased excretion of proteins and the presence of cells or casts, and measure BUN, serum creatinine or creatinine clearance periodically (FDA label, WARNINGS box). Obtain serial audiograms where feasible in patients old enough to be tested, particularly high-risk patients, and discontinue the drug or adjust the dosage if evidence of ototoxicity (dizziness, vertigo, tinnitus, roaring in the ears, hearing loss) or nephrotoxicity appears (FDA label, WARNINGS box). Assess kidney function by the usual methods prior to starting therapy and daily during treatment; if signs of renal irritation appear (casts, white or red cells, or albumin) hydration should be increased, a reduction in dosage may be desirable, and if azotemia increases or a progressive decrease in urinary output occurs, treatment should be stopped (FDA label, PRECAUTIONS - General). Perform bacteriological studies to identify the causative organism and its susceptibility, and base the decision to continue therapy on susceptibility results, severity of infection, patient response and the additional considerations in the WARNINGS box (FDA label, INDICATIONS AND USAGE). For ARIKAYCE, monitor for respiratory adverse reactions (hypersensitivity pneumonitis, hemoptysis, bronchospasm, exacerbation of underlying pulmonary disease), ototoxicity, nephrotoxicity and neuromuscular blockade (FDA label, ARIKAYCE, sections 5.1-5.8).
fields.patient_counselling: Advise patients that antibacterial drugs including amikacin should only be used to treat bacterial infections and do not treat viral infections such as the common cold; although it is common to feel better early in the course of therapy, the medication should be taken exactly as directed, because skipping doses or not completing the full course may decrease the effectiveness of the immediate treatment and increase the likelihood that bacteria will develop resistance (FDA label, PRECAUTIONS - Information for Patients). Tell patients that diarrhoea is a common problem caused by antibiotics which usually ends when the antibiotic is discontinued, and that watery and bloody stools (with or without stomach cramps and fever) can occur even as late as two or more months after the last dose of the antibiotic, in which case the physician should be contacted as soon as possible (FDA label, PRECAUTIONS - Information for Patients). Explain the need for blood tests to check kidney function and hearing during treatment, and advise the patient to report ringing in the ears, dizziness, vertigo, loss of balance, hearing loss, reduced urine output or swelling of the feet (FDA label, WARNINGS box and PRECAUTIONS - General). For ARIKAYCE, instruct the patient to use only the Lamira Nebulizer System, to shake the vial well for at least 10 to 15 seconds before opening, to take one 590 mg/8.4 mL vial once daily, not to double the dose if a dose is missed but to take the next dose the next day, and to report cough, haemoptysis, breathlessness, fever or rash promptly (FDA label, ARIKAYCE, sections 2.1, 2.2 and 17).
warnings: Patients treated with parenteral aminoglycosides should be under close clinical observation because of the potential ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity associated with their use; safety for treatment periods longer than 14 days has not been established (FDA label, WARNINGS box)

Neurotoxicity: vestibular and permanent bilateral auditory ototoxicity can occur, particularly in patients with pre-existing renal damage and in patients with normal renal function treated at higher doses and/or for periods longer than those recommended; high-frequency deafness usually occurs first and can be detected only by audiometric testing, and total or partial irreversible bilateral deafness may occur after the drug has been discontinued; other manifestations include numbness, skin tingling, muscle twitching and convulsions, and seizures may be exacerbated in patients with a prior history of seizure disorders (FDA label, WARNINGS box and OVERDOSAGE)

Nephrotoxicity: aminoglycosides are potentially nephrotoxic, and the risk is greater in patients with impaired renal function and in those who receive high doses or prolonged therapy (FDA label, WARNINGS box)

Neuromuscular blockade and respiratory paralysis have been reported following parenteral injection, topical instillation and oral use of aminoglycosides; the possibility should be considered if aminoglycosides are administered by any route, especially in patients receiving anaesthetics or neuromuscular blocking agents (tubocurarine, succinylcholine, decamethonium) or in patients receiving massive transfusions of citrate-anticoagulated blood; if blockage occurs, calcium salts may reverse these phenomena but mechanical respiratory assistance may be necessary (FDA label, WARNINGS box)

Risk of ototoxicity due to mitochondrial DNA variants: cases of ototoxicity with aminoglycosides have been observed in patients with certain variants in the mitochondrially encoded 12S rRNA gene (MT-RNR1), particularly the m.1555A>G variant, and ototoxicity occurred in some patients even when aminoglycoside serum levels were within the recommended range; mitochondrial DNA variants are present in less than 1% of the general US population, so in a patient with a known maternal history of ototoxicity due to aminoglycoside use or a known mitochondrial DNA variant, alternative treatments should be considered unless the increased risk of permanent hearing loss is outweighed by the severity of infection and the lack of safe and effective alternatives (FDA label, WARNINGS - Risk of Ototoxicity Due to Mitochondrial DNA Variants)

Aminoglycosides can cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman; aminoglycosides cross the placenta and there have been several reports of total, irreversible, bilateral congenital deafness in children whose mothers received streptomycin during pregnancy (FDA label, WARNINGS)

Contains sodium metabisulfite, a sulfite that may cause allergic-type reactions including anaphylactic symptoms and life-threatening or less severe asthmatic episodes in certain susceptible people; sulfite sensitivity is seen more frequently in asthmatic than nonasthmatic people (FDA label, WARNINGS)

Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhoea (CDAD) has been reported with use of nearly all antibacterial agents, including amikacin, and may range in severity from mild diarrhoea to fatal colitis; CDAD must be considered in all patients who present with diarrhoea following antibiotic use and can be reported over two months after the last dose (FDA label, WARNINGS - Clostridium difficile associated diarrhea)

ARIKAYCE boxed warning: ARIKAYCE has been associated with an increased risk of respiratory adverse reactions, including hypersensitivity pneumonitis, hemoptysis, bronchospasm and exacerbation of underlying pulmonary disease, that have led to hospitalizations in some cases (FDA label, ARIKAYCE, Boxed Warning)
precautions: Prescribing amikacin in the absence of a proven or strongly suspected bacterial infection or a prophylactic indication is unlikely to provide benefit and increases the risk of the development of drug-resistant bacteria (FDA label, PRECAUTIONS - General)

Aminoglycosides are quickly and almost totally absorbed when applied topically, except to the urinary bladder, and irreversible deafness, renal failure and death due to neuromuscular blockade have been reported after irrigation of surgical fields with an aminoglycoside preparation (FDA label, PRECAUTIONS - General)
Concurrent or serial use of other ototoxic or nephrotoxic agents should be avoided, systemically or topically, because of the potential for additive effects (FDA label, PRECAUTIONS - General)

Because amikacin is present in high concentrations in the renal excretory system, patients should be well hydrated to minimise chemical irritation of the renal tubules; if signs of renal irritation appear, hydration should be increased (FDA label, PRECAUTIONS - General)

Use with caution in patients with muscular disorders such as myasthenia gravis or parkinsonism, since these drugs may aggravate muscle weakness because of their potential curare-like effect on the neuromuscular junction (FDA label, PRECAUTIONS - General)
As with other antibiotics, use may result in overgrowth of nonsusceptible organisms, in which case appropriate therapy should be instituted (FDA label, PRECAUTIONS - General)

The vials are for single-dose only and any unused portion remaining in the vial should be discarded; parenteral drug products should be inspected visually for particulate matter and discoloration prior to administration (FDA label, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION and HOW SUPPLIED)
serious_adverse_reactions: Ototoxicity, including vestibular and permanent bilateral auditory damage, which is usually irreversible and may be preceded by high-frequency deafness detectable only by audiometric testing (FDA label, WARNINGS box and ADVERSE REACTIONS)
Nephrotoxicity, including elevated serum creatinine, albuminuria, casts, azotemia, oliguria, toxic nephropathy and acute renal failure (FDA label, ADVERSE REACTIONS - Nephrotoxicity)
Neuromuscular blockade with respiratory paralysis and possible need for mechanical ventilation (FDA label, WARNINGS box and ADVERSE REACTIONS)
Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhoea, which may be severe or fatal (FDA label, WARNINGS - Clostridium difficile associated diarrhea)
Hypersensitivity reactions including anaphylaxis and asthmatic episodes from sulfite (FDA label, WARNINGS and ADVERSE REACTIONS)
For ARIKAYCE: hypersensitivity pneumonitis, hemoptysis, bronchospasm and exacerbation of underlying pulmonary disease leading to hospitalisation (FDA label, ARIKAYCE, Boxed Warning)
fields.pregnancy_guidance: Aminoglycosides can cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman: they cross the placenta and there have been several reports of total, irreversible, bilateral congenital deafness in children whose mothers received streptomycin during pregnancy. Although serious side effects to the fetus or newborns have not been reported in the treatment of pregnant women with other aminoglycosides, the potential for harm exists. Reproduction studies of amikacin in rats and mice revealed no evidence of impaired fertility or harm to the fetus. There are no well-controlled studies in pregnant women, but investigational experience does not include any positive evidence of adverse effects to the fetus; if the drug is used during pregnancy, the patient should be apprised of the potential hazard to the fetus (FDA label, WARNINGS and PRECAUTIONS - Pregnancy/Teratogenic Effects). For ARIKAYCE, there are no data on use in pregnant women, but systemic exposure to aminoglycoside antibacterial drugs may be associated with total, irreversible, bilateral congenital deafness when administered to pregnant women, so pregnant women should be advised of the potential risk to the fetus; subcutaneous administration of amikacin to pregnant rats (up to 100 mg/kg/day) and mice (up to 400 mg/kg/day) during organogenesis was not associated with fetal malformations (FDA label, ARIKAYCE, section 8.1).
fields.lactation_guidance: It is not known whether amikacin is excreted in human milk. Because many drugs are excreted in human milk and because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in nursing infants from amikacin, a decision should be made whether to discontinue nursing or to discontinue the drug, taking into account the importance of the drug to the mother (FDA label, NURSING MOTHERS). For ARIKAYCE, there is no information regarding the presence of ARIKAYCE in human milk, the effects on the breastfed infant, or the effects on milk production after administration by inhalation, although limited published data on other routes of amikacin administration indicate that amikacin is present in human milk and systemic absorption following inhaled administration is expected to be low (FDA label, ARIKAYCE, section 8.2).
fields.overdose: In the event of overdosage or toxic reaction, peritoneal dialysis or hemodialysis will aid in the removal of amikacin from the blood; in the newborn infant, exchange transfusion may also be considered (FDA label, OVERDOSAGE). For ARIKAYCE, adverse reactions specifically associated with overdose have not been identified; acute toxicity should be treated with immediate withdrawal of ARIKAYCE and baseline tests of renal function, and hemodialysis may be helpful in removing amikacin from the body (FDA label, ARIKAYCE, section 10).
fields.pharmacokinetics: Amikacin is rapidly absorbed after intramuscular administration, with average peak serum concentrations of about 12, 16 and 21 mcg/mL one hour after single doses of 250 mg (3.7 mg/kg), 375 mg (5 mg/kg) and 500 mg (7.5 mg/kg) respectively, and serum levels of about 0.3, 1.2 and 2.1 mcg/mL at 10 hours. With normal renal function about 91.9% of an intramuscular dose is excreted unchanged in the urine in the first 8 hours and 98.2% within 24 hours. A single 500 mg (7.5 mg/kg) intravenous dose infused over 30 minutes produced a mean peak serum concentration of 38 mcg/mL at the end of the infusion, with 84% of the dose excreted in the urine in 9 hours and about 94% within 24 hours. In normal adult subjects the mean serum half-life is slightly over 2 hours, the mean total apparent volume of distribution is 24 litres (28% of body weight), serum protein binding ranges from 0 to 11%, the mean serum clearance rate is about 100 mL/min and the renal clearance rate is 94 mL/min. Amikacin is excreted primarily by glomerular filtration, so renal function must be monitored carefully and the dosage adjusted accordingly. Following the recommended dose, therapeutic levels are found in bone, heart, gallbladder and lung tissue in addition to significant concentrations in urine, bile, sputum, bronchial secretions, interstitial, pleural and synovial fluids; spinal fluid levels are approximately 10 to 20% of serum concentrations and may reach 50% when the meninges are inflamed. Amikacin crosses the placental barrier: peak fetal serum concentration is about 16% of the peak maternal serum concentration, with maternal and fetal half-lives of about 2 and 3.7 hours (FDA label, CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY - Intramuscular Administration, Intravenous Administration and General).
clinical_pearls: Amikacin is one of the few aminoglycosides that resists degradation by aminoglycoside-inactivating enzymes affecting gentamicin, tobramycin and kanamycin, and it has documented activity against gentamicin- and tobramycin-resistant Gram-negative organisms - but this does not remove the need for susceptibility testing (FDA label, Microbiology and INDICATIONS AND USAGE).

Safety for treatment periods longer than 14 days has not been established, and the usual recommended duration is 7 to 10 days, with re-evaluation if treatment beyond 10 days is considered (FDA label, WARNINGS box and DOSAGE).

Aminoglycoside ototoxicity is usually irreversible and may be silent: high-frequency hearing loss is detected only by audiometric testing, so serial audiograms are recommended in patients old enough to be tested, particularly high-risk patients (FDA label, WARNINGS box).
Therapeutic drug monitoring targets are explicit: avoid peak levels above 35 mcg/mL and trough levels above 10 mcg/mL (FDA label, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION).

In patients with impaired renal function the label offers two validated strategies - normal dose at prolonged intervals (interval in hours = serum creatinine x 9) or reduced dose at fixed intervals scaled to creatinine clearance - and neither should be used during dialysis (FDA label, DOSAGE - Intramuscular Administration for Patients with Impaired Renal Function).

ARIKAYCE is a different formulation and a different indication (inhaled liposomal amikacin for refractory MAC lung disease) with its own boxed warning and its own administration device; it is not interchangeable with injectable amikacin (FDA label, ARIKAYCE, sections 1 and 2.1).
black_box_warnings: ARIKAYCE: RISK OF INCREASED RESPIRATORY ADVERSE REACTIONS - ARIKAYCE has been associated with an increased risk of respiratory adverse reactions, including hypersensitivity pneumonitis, hemoptysis, bronchospasm and exacerbation of underlying pulmonary disease, that have led to hospitalizations in some cases (FDA label, ARIKAYCE, Boxed Warning). Note: the injectable amikacin sulfate injection label itself carries a prominent WARNINGS section but no boxed warning.
fields.renal_dose_adjustment: Two methods, based on creatinine clearance or serum creatinine, are given; neither should be used when dialysis is being performed, and both must be used with careful clinical and laboratory observation (FDA label, DOSAGE - Intramuscular Administration for Patients with Impaired Renal Function). Normal dose at prolonged intervals: if creatinine clearance is not available and the patient is stable, multiply the serum creatinine (mg/100 mL) by 9 to obtain the dosing interval in hours, for example a serum creatinine of 2 mg/100 mL gives a single 7.5 mg/kg dose every 18 hours. Reduced dose at fixed interval: give a normal loading dose of 7.5 mg/kg, then for maintenance doses every 12 hours multiply the observed creatinine clearance by the calculated loading dose and divide by the normal creatinine clearance; a rough alternative is to divide the normally recommended dose by the patient's serum creatinine. For ARIKAYCE, amikacin has not been studied in patients with renal impairment, but given the low systemic exposure following inhalation, clinically relevant accumulation is unlikely; renal function should be monitored in patients with known or suspected renal impairment, including elderly patients (FDA label, ARIKAYCE, section 8.7).
fields.hepatic_dose_adjustment: The amikacin sulfate injection label does not specify a hepatic dose adjustment; amikacin is excreted primarily by glomerular filtration rather than hepatic metabolism. For ARIKAYCE, amikacin has not been studied in patients with hepatic impairment and no dose adjustments based on hepatic impairment are required, since amikacin is not hepatically metabolised (FDA label, ARIKAYCE, section 8.6).
fields.administration_instructions: Amikacin Sulfate Injection may be given intramuscularly or intravenously. The patient's pretreatment body weight should be obtained for calculation of the correct dosage, and renal function should be estimated by serum creatinine concentration or calculation of the endogenous creatinine clearance rate, with reassessment periodically during therapy. For intravenous use, add the contents of a 500 mg vial to 100 or 200 mL of sterile diluent such as 0.9% sodium chloride injection or 5% dextrose injection, or any of the listed compatible solutions, and administer to adults over 30 to 60 minutes; infants should receive a 1 to 2 hour infusion. Amikacin should not be physically premixed with other drugs but should be administered separately according to the recommended dose and route. The solution is stable for 24 hours at room temperature at concentrations of 0.25 and 5 mg/mL in 5% dextrose, 5% dextrose with 0.2% or 0.45% sodium chloride, 0.9% sodium chloride, lactated Ringer's, Normosol-M or Normosol-R in 5% dextrose. Vials are for single-dose only and any unused portion should be discarded; store at 20 to 25 degrees C, excursions permitted between 15 and 30 degrees C. ARIKAYCE: administer with the Lamira Nebulizer System only; bring the vial to room temperature before use, shake it well for at least 10 to 15 seconds until the contents appear uniform and well mixed, then pour the contents into the nebulizer medication reservoir; if a daily dose is missed, administer the next dose the next day and do not double the dose (FDA label, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION, HOW SUPPLIED; ARIKAYCE, sections 2.1 and 2.2).

notes: The table stores this agent as 'Amikacin' with brand_names ['Amikacin Sulfate']; amikacin sulfate injection is a generic product, and the only aminoglycoside brand product listed on DailyMed for amikacin is ARIKAYCE (amikacin liposome inhalation suspension), so brand_names has been set to that verified brand. Two different amikacin products are covered: injectable amikacin sulfate (Mullan Pharmaceutical label, revised 04/2025) and ARIKAYCE, an inhaled liposomal formulation for refractory MAC lung disease with its own boxed warning, its own dosing and the Lamira nebulizer device. The injectable label has a prominent WARNINGS section (ototoxicity, nephrotoxicity, neuromuscular blockade) but no US boxed warning, so the only boxed warning recorded belongs to ARIKAYCE. Kenya Essential Medicines List 2023 is included for the national context used in this app. The Kenya list also places amikacin injection at level of use 4.
